speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing agitation and have a yellowish discoloration of your skin and eyes; have you noticed any pain in your upper right abdomen or changes in your urine color recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis B with Drug-Induced Hepatotoxicity (Cocaine/Alcohol). The clinical picture of agitation, jaundice, and a history of high-risk sexual behavior and substance use in a previously healthy 20-year-old male is highly suggestive of acute viral hepatitis, likely Hepatitis B, potentially exacerbated by toxic ingestion. I will confirm this with liver function tests and serology.
